April: The Season Kicks Off

April is when the UK motorcycle touring season truly begins. Daylight stretches to 8pm, temperatures regularly reach double figures, and the landscape transforms with spring growth. It's an exciting, energising month to ride.

Conditions

  • Temperature: Average 7-14°C. Warm days can reach 18°C in the south. Scottish highlands remain cool (5-10°C).
  • Daylight: 6am-8pm. Finally enough light for a proper day ride after work.
  • April showers: The name isn't an accident. Expect rain showers interspersed with sunshine. A waterproof layer is essential.

Where to Ride in April

  • Cotswolds: Spring flowers, green countryside, and quiet roads before summer tourists arrive.
  • Welsh Valleys: The Wye Valley and Usk Valley are at their most beautiful in spring — fresh green leaves, bluebells in the woodland, lambs in the fields.
  • Dorset and Devon: Mild coastal temperatures and the first beach-side coffee of the year.
  • Peak District: The moors are greening up and the passes are clear of winter grit.

Easter Riding

Easter falls in April most years and offers a long weekend perfect for the first tour of the season. Popular areas will be busy — book accommodation and plan routes that avoid the honey-pot villages on Easter weekend.

April Bike Prep

  • Full service if not done in winter — oil, filters, coolant check
  • Fresh tyres if your old ones are marginal — start the season with good rubber
  • Test all electrics — indicators, brake lights, horn
  • Charge and test your intercom, GPS, and phone mount systems
  • Clean your riding gear — reproofing waterproof textiles restores their water resistance
April is the month of possibility. The whole touring season stretches ahead. Use April rides to shake off winter rust, test new gear, and start planning summer tours. Every April ride is an investment in the months to come.

April Destination Ideas

The Cotswolds in April are picture-perfect — blossom on the trees, green fields, and the honey-stone villages at their most photogenic. The roads between Stow-on-the-Wold, Bourton-on-the-Water, and Broadway flow beautifully and the traffic is lighter than summer.

The Welsh Valleys warm up in April, making the Wye Valley, Usk Valley, and Brecon Beacons accessible and beautiful. The waterfalls in the Brecon Beacons are at their most impressive after spring rain, and the roads through the national park are some of the finest in Britain.

Enjoying Lambing Season

Despite the hazards, lambing season is one of the most charming times to ride through farming country. The sight of lambs playing in spring sunshine across green fields, with mountain backdrops and clear skies, epitomises the British countryside at its most appealing.

Many farms welcome visitors during lambing season. Farm cafes serve excellent home-cooked food, and some farms offer lambing experiences where you can help with feeding. These make unique touring stops that connect you with the agricultural life that shapes the landscapes you ride through. Read our UK Motorcycle Riding in January: Winter Riding Guide guide for more. April showers are frequent, so a waterproof layer is essential.
The Cotswolds, Welsh valleys, Dorset, Devon and the Peak District all shine before summer crowds arrive.
Easter usually falls in April, offering the first long-weekend tour, so book accommodation early.

faq.q: Is April a good month for motorcycle touring?
faq.a: April is when the UK touring season truly begins. Daylight stretches to 8pm, temperatures regularly reach double figures and the landscape transforms with spring growth. It is an energising month, though April showers are frequent so a waterproof layer is essential. Use April rides to shake off winter rust, test new gear and start planning summer tours.

faq.q: Where should I ride in April?
faq.a: The Cotswolds are picture-perfect with blossom and lighter traffic than summer, and the roads between Stow-on-the-Wold, Bourton-on-the-Water and Broadway flow beautifully. The Welsh valleys warm up, making the Wye Valley, Usk Valley and Brecon Beacons accessible, with waterfalls at their most impressive after spring rain. Dorset, Devon and the Peak District are also excellent.

faq.q: How should I plan around Easter in April?
faq.a: Easter falls in April most years and offers a long weekend perfect for the first tour of the season. Popular areas will be busy, so book accommodation and plan routes that avoid the honey-pot villages over the Easter weekend. Pack for unpredictable weather, from cold snaps to warm spells, and have a wet-weather alternative for each day.

faq.q: What bike prep does April need?
faq.a: Give the bike a full service if it was not done in winter, covering oil, filters and a coolant check. Fit fresh tyres if the old ones are marginal so you start the season with good rubber, test all electrics including indicators, brake lights and horn, and check your intercom, GPS and phone mounts. Clean and reproof your riding gear to restore water resistance.

faq.q: Is lambing season still a factor in April?
faq.a: Yes, lambing continues into April and remains a road hazard in farming country, so keep speeds down through rural areas. It is also charming: lambs playing in spring sunshine epitomise the British countryside. Many farms welcome visitors, with farm cafes serving home-cooked food, making unique touring stops that connect you with the landscapes you ride through.
